title: Computed Tomography (CT) of the Chest with Contrast
description: Medicare coverage criteria for diagnostic chest CT with contrast. Requires abnormal chest radiograph (suspicious solitary pulmonary nodule > 6 mm, mass, lymphadenopathy, pleural effusion), hemoptysis with risk factors, or evaluation of interstitial lung disease.

criteria.name: Abnormal Chest Radiograph (Solitary Nodule > 6 mm or Mass)
criteria.description: Preceding chest X-ray documenting indeterminate solitary pulmonary nodule > 6 mm, hilar/mediastinal widening, lung mass, or unresolving infiltrate.
criteria.clinical_intent: Objective abnormal baseline plain film finding
criteria.source_text_excerpt: Evaluation of pulmonary, mediastinal, pleural and chest wall infections and their complications

criteria.name: Unexplained Hemoptysis or Interstitial Lung Disease Evaluation
criteria.description: Documented gross hemoptysis in patient aged >= 40 or >= 30 pack-year smoking history, or clinical signs of progressive interstitial lung disease.
criteria.source_text_excerpt: For characterizing and follow-up evaluation of interstitial and alveolar lung disease due to idiopathic, allergic, collagen-vascular, environmental or other causes

criteria.name: Uncomplicated Acute Bronchitis Without Radiograph Exclusion
criteria.description: CT chest requested for simple acute bronchitis or viral upper respiratory infection without preceding chest X-ray.
criteria.clinical_intent: Prevent high-dose radiation CT for simple uncomplicated viral illness
criteria.source_text_excerpt: The chest x-ray and/or physical examination should be used to evaluate patients who present with signs and/or symptoms suggestive of chest pathology prior to proceeding to a CT scan.

cms_reference.notes: Verified from official CMS Coverage API /v1/data/lcd?lcdid=33459. Replaces MISMATCH (previously cited L34417 was CT of the Head).
